l6: Is a private chauffeur more expensive than Uber in Miami?
l7: Often, private chauffeur service costs more than standard rideshare during normal demand. Rideshare pricing changes in real time, while a chauffeur quote is provided in advance. The best value depends on the route, vehicle category, pickup requirements, and level of coordination needed.
l8: Is Uber Black the same as a chauffeur service?
l9: Not exactly. Uber Black is a commercially licensed premium ride category, and Uber Reserve may allow advance scheduling. A dedicated private chauffeur service differs mainly in the direct provider relationship: pickup details, luggage requirements, stops, passenger communication, and any return itinerary can be coordinated with the same transportation company before the trip.
l10: Does a private chauffeur track my flight?
l11: Yes. We monitor the flight status using the flight number provided with the reservation. If the flight arrives early or is delayed, we adjust the pickup coordination accordingly and keep the booking contact informed when necessary.
l12: What happens if my flight is delayed?
l13: We monitor the flight's actual arrival status and adjust pickup coordination accordingly. Expected baggage-claim or customs time, included waiting time, and any charges for extended delays should be confirmed as part of the reservation.
l14: Where does the chauffeur meet me at MIA, FLL, or DJT?
l15: The specific pickup point is agreed at booking and depends on the airport, terminal, and any regulations in effect that day — curbside, or a meet-and-greet point inside the terminal if requested.
l16: Can the driver meet me inside the terminal?
l17: Meet-and-greet inside the terminal may be available when requested and confirmed in advance, subject to airport access rules, parking conditions, and the agreed service plan.
l18: How much luggage fits in a Chevrolet Suburban?
l19: Capacity depends on the number of passengers, suitcase dimensions, child seats, strollers, golf bags, and whether every seating row is required. Send the passenger count and a realistic bag count before booking so ONYX can confirm whether the Suburban is suitable.
l20: Can I request a child seat?
l21: Child-seat requests must be discussed before booking. Availability, seat type, installation responsibility, and any additional charge are confirmed as part of the reservation.
l22: Can I book transportation for someone else?
l23: Yes. We can coordinate with both the person booking and the passenger, which is common for family members, clients, or employees flying in separately.
l24: How far in advance should I book?
l25: Booking as early as possible gives you the best chance of confirming the preferred vehicle and pickup method. Same-day requests may be available, while peak dates, group travel, and meet-and-greet service should be arranged earlier whenever possible.
l26: Do you cover FLL to Aventura and Sunny Isles?
l27: Yes. ONYX provides pre-arranged transfers between FLL and Aventura, Sunny Isles, Hallandale Beach, Hollywood, Bal Harbour, and other destinations across Miami-Dade and Broward counties.

h4: Private chauffeur vs. Uber and Lyft in Miami: which airport ride is right for you?
h5: Rideshare helps you request a car. A private chauffeur service manages the trip. Here is the honest, factor-by-factor difference for Miami-area airport arrivals.
h6: Quick answer: rideshare is usually the better choice for a spontaneous, lower-cost local trip. A pre-booked chauffeur is usually the better choice when planning, timing, luggage capacity, airport coordination, or direct communication matter more than the lowest possible fare — families with luggage, executives on a tight schedule, international or late-night arrivals, and anyone booking transportation for someone else.
h7: Neither option is always better. This page compares them factor by factor so you can decide based on your specific arrival, not a general claim that one wins in every case.

h65: Uber Black upgrades the ride. A private chauffeur service manages the trip.
h66: Uber Black can provide a commercially licensed professional driver and an eligible premium vehicle, and Uber Reserve may allow a passenger to schedule the trip in advance. The key distinction is not simply the vehicle or whether a reservation exists. With a dedicated private provider, the passenger or booking contact works directly with the same transportation company to plan the pickup, luggage requirements, stops, and follow-up communication.
h67: A dedicated chauffeur service coordinates the arrival, not only the vehicle. You know who is responsible for the route, and luggage requirements, requested child-seat arrangements, and additional stops can be discussed before booking — with one direct contact instead of only an in-app interface. Uber published its own comparison of Uber Black, chauffeur service, and limo service in July 2026 — useful context on how Uber frames the difference, independent of this page.
h69: MIA, FLL, and DJT: the practical difference
h70: One operator covers all three airports across our full service area — Miami-Dade, Broward, and Palm Beach counties. With rideshare, the exact pickup zone, level, and door are assigned by the app and can vary by terminal and by day. With a pre-arranged chauffeur, the pickup method and communication plan are confirmed before arrival, and remain subject to current airport regulations.
h72: Ride-app pickups at MIA are available at designated locations on the Arrivals and Departures levels. Passengers should check the app for the assigned level, pickup zone, and door number — see MIA's official taxis and ride-app page. Details on our MIA transfer page →
h74: FLL ride-app pickup locations vary by terminal and may include designated curbside areas or the Palm Garage. Passengers should follow current airport signs and the pickup location shown in their app — see Broward County's official FLL rideshare page. Details on our FLL transfer page →
h75: DJT — formerly Palm Beach International Airport
h76: Ride-app pickup is currently on the outer curb of the third-floor Departures level, which may require moving up from baggage claim — confirmed on the airport's official site. The airport's passenger-facing IATA code changed from PBI to DJT on August 18, 2026. Details on our DJT transfer page →
h78: What a confirmed pickup point looks like.
h79: When meet-and-greet is requested and confirmed in advance, your chauffeur is inside the terminal with your name confirmed — not one face in a line of drivers at the curb.
a6: ONYX chauffeur holding a tablet with a client's name, meeting a passenger inside the airport terminal
h81: Five situations where the difference actually shows up
h82: Family arrival. A family of five lands with six suitcases and two carry-ons. Confirming vehicle and luggage capacity before the flight avoids deciding between ride categories after landing.
h83: Executive arrival. A call is scheduled 30 minutes after landing. The value is not a nicer SUV — it is knowing the pickup method, driver contact, and destination before the aircraft arrives.
h84: Booking for someone else. The person paying is not always the passenger. A pre-arranged service can communicate with both the booking contact and the traveler directly.
h85: Cruise transfer. Airport-to-port trips run against a fixed embarkation schedule, so a cancellation or vehicle mismatch has more consequences than a casual city ride.
h86: Late-night international arrival. After immigration, baggage claim, and a long flight, the passenger should not have to start solving transportation logistics from scratch.
h88: Bags handled, not negotiated at the curb.
h89: Luggage assistance is part of the pickup, not an afterthought — useful the moment you land with a briefcase, a laptop bag, and a flight that just got in.
a7: ONYX chauffeur assisting a passenger with a bag beside the Suburban outside a South Florida hotel
h91: Safety is not only about the driver.
h92: Transportation safety also comes down to knowing the vehicle in advance, confirming passenger and luggage capacity, having a direct point of contact, reducing curbside confusion, and making sure whoever booked the ride knows when the passenger has actually been picked up.
h93: What we can confirm for ONYX specifically, as part of what we call the Onyx Standard: commercially insured operation, active Miami-Dade chauffeur registration, a confirmed vehicle for every accepted booking, and one direct contact for the whole trip.
